questions.question: What should happen to RFC-0019 now that only its CI lane is still open?

options.label: Leave as Draft (Recommended)
options.description: No change now. ID-266 rewrites it when the CI lane starts, after BK-408 changes the pass conditions. The Status block already says what was replaced.

options.label: Start BK-408 now
options.description: Change the Roadmap pass conditions to judge on net time saved, as the first step toward rewriting the CI lane. Small item, done on its own branch.

options.label: Withdraw and replace
options.description: Mark RFC-0019 Withdrawn, keeping its Phase 0 history, and write a new RFC for only the CI lane, possibly reusing fast_gate.py. ID-266 and BK-408 then point to the new RFC.

options.label: Change exits 2–3 only (Recommended)
options.description: Rewrite the Phase 2 and 3 pass conditions and D7.4's zero-escape sentence around net time saved, with each escape costed as one full run (the bucket-rules / fast-gate standard). Keep Phase 0's row as it ran, with a note. Close BK-408. Selector, lane design and full rewrite stay with ID-266.

options.label: Also mark local phases replaced
options.description: Do the above, and also mark the Phase 1 and Phase 2 local deliverables (pilot selector, local fast target) as replaced by hatch run fast, so the Roadmap only describes the CI path. Bigger change that starts on ID-266's rewrite.

options.label: Change all three, Phase 0 too
options.description: Apply the new standard to Phase 0's row as well. This rewrites the bar Phase 0 was actually measured against, so the record of its stop decision changes after the fact.

options.label: Measure the wait first (Recommended)
options.description: Script over about 30 days of PR CI runs: how long CI was still running when the next push, review or merge happened. Small result: close ID-266 as decided against, with a reopen condition. Large result: speed up the full run first, then revisit. No CI changes; roughly a few hours of work.

options.label: Shadow trial (RFC-0019 Phase 3)
options.description: Build a CI selector, log what it would pick on every push while the full gate still runs, then judge after a fixed period on net time saved. Answers selection quality, but costs a CI-side selector before anything is learned.

options.label: Close it now
options.description: Decide against ID-266 today on the figures above (4–4.7 min code-PR runs, free minutes, CI runs alongside review), with a reopen condition. Fastest, but rests on a sample, not a measurement.

options.label: Speed up full CI instead
options.description: Leave ID-266 parked and work on making the full gate itself faster (shard timing refresh, audit-022 M2/P5). This helps every push and the merge head.

questions.question: What should happen to ID-266 given the history?

options.label: Decide against + record (Recommended)
options.description: Move ID-266 to BACKLOG-DONE § Decided against, citing this measurement with a reopen condition (code-PR median CI above ~10 min, the repo going private, or the waiting excess growing). Commit the two scripts and a short research snapshot so the figures can be re-derived (principle 9). Mark RFC-0019 Withdrawn or Superseded in the same PR.

options.label: Decide against, no research doc
options.description: Same close, but the entry cites the figures and the commands inline only, without committing the scripts. Smaller PR; the derivation isn't re-runnable from the repo.

options.label: Park it, re-measure later
options.description: Keep ID-266 open with this result in its dossier and a date to re-run the history script, e.g. after the next release. Nothing is closed yet.

options.label: Pivot to a faster full gate
options.description: Decide against ID-266 as in the first option, and also file or start the full-run speedup (audit-022 M2/P5 shard timings), which addresses the 36.6 h of merge waiting.
